title: Roomcode Tactics
user: Two remote friends who want a low-stakes, room-code tactical game that survives a deployment/reconnect and does not demand a persistent account or a huge concurrent community.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A developer asks how to build a turn-based multiplayer browser game in 2025, specifically concerned that deployments will interrupt ongoing games.
A 2026 itch.io devlog presents a free browser multiplayer sandbox, confirming browser-native multiplayer remains an active indie format rather than an abandoned distribution channel.

recurrence: The HN request exposes the reliability constraint of browser turn-based play; the independent itch.io thread confirms ongoing browser-multiplayer experimentation in 2026.
current_workaround: Use Board Game Arena/Discord/Steam, wait for a friend to install a client, or build a bespoke multiplayer prototype whose sessions break during deployment.
incumbents_and_gap: Board Game Arena has breadth and accounts; online tactics games usually require a client, ladder, or community population. A tiny asynchronous room can avoid matchmaking and still offer meaningful interaction.
smallest_useful_product: A two-player, room-code asynchronous tactics game on a 7×7 map. Each side gets five turns over up to 24 hours, submits a simultaneous move, and receives a short animated resolution; a match ends in 10–15 decisions. Maps rotate through weather and objective rules. Non-goals: real-time combat, public matchmaking, guilds, global ladder, or long-lived worlds.
success_measure: At least 60% of created rooms receive a second player move, 40% complete, and fewer than 2% of completed games require support for an interrupted deployment/reconnect.
monetization: free — room-code sharing needs a zero-friction first match; one-time map-pack support can be tested after completion rates are proven.
constraints: Persist moves and deterministic state before response; use idempotent turn submission and signed opaque room tokens; throttle abuse without forcing accounts; no copyrighted board-game rules or maps.
why_distinct: The design is intentionally a resilient, finite correspondence game—not a live-service tactics clone with matchmaking.
